stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
The model is optimized for local coding agents and features native DFlash and image input support via Ollama's MLX engine.

stories.title: Now Google says it might use your Gmail and Google Photos data to target ads
stories.author: Jess Weatherbed
bullet_points: Google updated its privacy policy to potentially use Gmail and Google Photos data for targeted advertising.
This change specifically relates to the use of personalized AI features within Google services.
The update creates an exception to Google's previous commitment not to use Drive, Gmail, or Photos for personalized ads.

stories.title: Agents should never hold your API keys. NVIDIA just open-sourced the runtime that enforces it
stories.author: slabb
bullet_points: NVIDIA open-sourced OpenShell, a new runtime designed to enhance agent security.
The runtime enforces kernel-level sandboxing for agent fleets, preventing them from storing API keys.
Security policies are rigorously checked by a Z3 SMT prover before requiring human approval.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The tags confirm its relevance within the broader AI/ML ecosystem (transformers, llama).

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under key AI/ML domains including transformers, llama, and text-generation.
This indicates ongoing community interest and benchmarking activity around a major open-source LLM.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B parameter open model, is now accessible via Ollama.
The model is specifically designed for autonomous agents capable of multi-step tasks and tool calling.
It emphasizes running complex AI workloads locally on user hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved within Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance, specifically using the Aider polyglot benchmark, shows up to a 90% speed increase.

stories.title: Elon Musk’s dangerous grip on outer space
stories.author: Georgina Torbet
bullet_points: SpaceX's Starshield, used by Ukraine, was throttled to block high-speed terminals.
This throttling disabled Ukrainian interceptors designed to counter Russian drones.
The service disruption potentially aided Russia by making it easier to attack Ukrainian energy infrastructure.

stories.title: Feds want robotaxis to signal ‘I’m driving’ with cyan-colored lights
stories.author: Andrew J. Hawkins
bullet_points: The NHTSA has mandated a specific visual indicator for autonomous vehicles.
Robotaxis must now use cyan-colored lights to signal that they are operating without a human driver.
This decision resolves a long-standing regulatory debate regarding how driverless cars should communicate their status to the public.

stories.title: SpaceX’s mobile carrier push reportedly involves tapping into 80,000 cell sites
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: SpaceX is reportedly moving into the mobile carrier space to compete with major incumbents like Verizon and T-Mobile.
The strategy involves securing access to a massive infrastructure footprint, specifically targeting 80,000 cell sites.
SpaceX is reportedly in discussions with Crown Castle Inc., a major owner of cell tower infrastructure.

stories.title: Intel gets waiver after worries fuzzy US ban on foreign-made robots may hit fabs
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Intel secured a waiver regarding potential US restrictions on foreign-made robots.
The waiver addresses concerns about a fuzzy US ban impacting semiconductor fabrication plants (fabs).
Intel emphasizes that foreign-made robotic vehicles are essential for maintaining US chip production capabilities.

stories.title: Ukraine learns to fight without Starlink as Musk plays politics with satellites
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Ukraine is actively developing alternative drone and war-fighting technologies.
The shift is a direct response to perceived political interference or reliance on Starlink.
The story highlights the geopolitical risks associated with critical commercial satellite infrastructure in conflict zones.

stories.title: EpiSEM-Bench: Evaluating Safety and Evidence Recovery in LLM Agents under Missing Evidence
stories.author: Shuang Qiu
bullet_points: Introduces EpiSEM-Bench, a new benchmark specifically designed to test LLM agents when critical safety facts are missing from tool responses.
Addresses a critical vulnerability where agents can perform prohibited actions even with benign user requests if environmental facts are omitted.
The benchmark includes 300 matched unsafe/safe task pairs across six domains to evaluate safety boundaries and evidence recovery.

stories.title: VERA: A Responsible AI Dashboard for Assessing LLM Deployments in Light of the EU AI Act
stories.author: Jérôme Lebecq
bullet_points: VERA introduces a Responsible AI Dashboard designed to help institutions comply with the EU AI Act when deploying LLMs.
The system translates the EU AI Act into 18 technical requirements, organized under six principle groups.
It provides measurable benchmarks for twelve of the technical requirements, bridging the gap between technical evidence and non-technical approval processes.

stories.title: EpiSEM-Bench: Evaluating Safety and Evidence Recovery in LLM Agents under Missing Evidence
stories.author: Shuang Qiu
bullet_points: Introduces EpiSEM-Bench, a new benchmark designed to test LLM agents' safety when critical evidence is missing from tool responses.
Addresses a critical vulnerability where agents can perform prohibited actions even with benign user requests if safety facts are omitted by tools.
The benchmark comprises 300 matched unsafe/safe task pairs across six domains, focusing on evaluating unsafe execution and evidence recovery.

stories.title: The Geometry of Metaphor: Probing and Steering Metaphor Representations in Large Language Models
stories.author: Martha Lewis
bullet_points: The research uses mechanistic interpretability to probe how Large Language Models (LLMs) represent metaphor.
The study successfully demonstrates the ability to causally steer LLM outputs on classification tasks across different parts of speech.
The findings indicate that these interpretability techniques can be applied to control LLM generation tasks, offering new avenues for model steering.

stories.title: Clef is available on Ollama's cloud
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Clef, a 27B multimodal decision model from Cloudflare, is now integrated with Ollama.
Users have the option to run the Clef model either locally or via Ollama's cloud infrastructure.
This integration expands the capabilities of Ollama by adding a powerful, large-scale multimodal model.

stories.title: Reflection's Beam is freely available on Ollama for a limited time
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Reflection's open-weight model, Beam, is now available on the Ollama platform.
Beam is specifically engineered for tasks in software engineering, reasoning, and agentic workflows.
The model is currently offered free of charge for a limited promotional period via Ollama Cloud.

stories.title: Run AI agents safely with Ollama and Fly.io
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama enables the use of local AI models within a cloud environment.
Fly.io provides the cloud infrastructure for safely running these AI agents.
The integration focuses on enhancing the security and deployment of AI agents.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These new models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free decision-making based on text input.
The models provide probabilistic answers to yes/no questions, choices, and scoring.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-source LLM ecosystems.

stories.title: Jack Dorsey’s Block made an AI model that talks to you like an awkward new friend
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Block (Jack Dorsey's company) has released a new AI model named Dessa.
Dessa was trained exclusively on human conversation data, aiming for a natural conversational style.
The model's demonstrations highlight its conversational nature, sometimes resulting in awkward or uncanny interactions.

stories.title: Switch 2 security takes a hit as hackers unlock homebrew access
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: The upcoming Switch 2 console is facing security vulnerabilities.
Hackers have exploited an integer overflow in the 'SmileBasic' interpreter.
This exploit allows unauthorized homebrew access to the system.

stories.title: Direct Pass@$k$ Optimization for Thought Pruning: Balancing Quality and Diversity in Test-Time Reasoning
stories.author: Meisam Razaviyayn
bullet_points: The paper addresses the computational cost of test-time scaling in reasoning models, where many candidate solutions are generated.
It introduces 'Direct Pass@$k$ Optimization' as a method to efficiently prune candidate solutions after only a short prefix is generated.
The research focuses on balancing the quality (accuracy) and diversity of the surviving candidates during the pruning process.

stories.title: METTA: Memory-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation for Meta-Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Mahdieh Soleymani Baghshah
bullet_points: Introduces METTA, a new framework for Memory-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation in Meta-Reinforcement Learning.
Addresses the challenge of representing long interaction histories in meta-RL, contrasting classical recurrent and high-cost transformer approaches.
Proposes a method to decompose the fast adaptation phase, aiming to improve efficiency and memory usage during task adaptation.

stories.title: Low-Bit N-Gram Embeddings for Language Models
stories.author: Wenyu Du
bullet_points: The paper addresses the significant memory overhead associated with n-gram embedding tables in modern open-weight language models.
Current models, like DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, utilize large n-gram memory tables (e.g., 196 billion parameters) for performance enhancement.
The research aims to investigate methods for reducing the memory footprint of these embeddings while maintaining or preserving model performance.

stories.title: Causal Chain of Thought: Mitigating Attention Leakage via Context Isolation
stories.author: Martin Gjoreski
bullet_points: Addresses a fundamental limitation of Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting: the generated reasoning steps may not causally drive the final prediction.
Introduces CausalCoT, a new inference framework designed to enforce causal transparency during model reasoning.
Mitigates 'attention leakage' in standard autoregressive models where dense attention allows for plausible but ungrounded justifications.

stories.title: Questioning Instrumental Convergence in RLVR: Checkpoint Evidence from OLMo-3
stories.author: Caleb Petterson
bullet_points: The paper investigates 'Instrumental Convergence' (IC), a theory suggesting advanced AI agents will develop power-seeking subgoals (e.g., self-preservation, resource acquisition).
It focuses on Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) stages of LLMs, as this is where behavior is directly optimized against an objective.
The research uses checkpoint evidence from OLMo-3 to question or test the predictions made by the Instrumental Convergence hypothesis.

stories.title: Sensorimotor Alignment: A Platonic Proxy for Embodied Policy Success
stories.author: Chen Wei
bullet_points: The paper proposes using cheap offline proxies to evaluate robotic foundation models, moving away from expensive closed-loop rollouts.
It introduces the Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH), suggesting that different modalities (vision, language, motion) converge toward a shared statistical model of reality as models improve.
The core question investigated is whether motion trajectories function as another modality that should converge with sensory representations in highly capable embodied models.

stories.title: Phase Transition from Random Features to Fully Trainable Networks
stories.author: Shijun Zhang
bullet_points: The research explores a novel intermediate model, 'partially trainable neural networks,' situated between fixed random features and fully adaptive networks.
The paper quantifies a 'phase transition' pattern in approximation bounds and training errors as the network structure changes.
The observed training error behavior shows an initial rapid improvement followed by diminishing returns, sensitive to initialization mismatch.

stories.title: SpectralCanary: Embarrassingly Simple Low-Frequency Traces for T2I Dataset-Use Auditing
stories.author: Furong Huang
bullet_points: Introduces SpectralCanary, a new method for auditing if Text-to-Image (T2I) models were fine-tuned on specific image datasets.
Addresses the challenge that models can absorb dataset characteristics without reproducing training images.
Aims to improve upon existing auditing techniques by balancing verifiability, fidelity, robustness, and deployability.

stories.title: METTA: Memory-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation for Meta-Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Mahdieh Soleymani Baghshah
bullet_points: Introduces METTA, a new framework for Memory-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation in Meta-Reinforcement Learning.
Addresses the challenge of representing long interaction histories in meta-RL agents, contrasting recurrent and transformer approaches.
Aims to improve fast adaptation to unseen tasks by efficiently managing task evidence over extended interaction histories.

stories.title: Causal Chain of Thought: Mitigating Attention Leakage via Context Isolation
stories.author: Martin Gjoreski
bullet_points: Addresses a core limitation of Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting: the generated reasoning steps may not causally drive the final prediction.
Introduces CausalCoT, a new inference framework designed to enforce causal transparency in large language model reasoning.
Mitigates 'attention leakage' by isolating context during the step-by-step generation process, preventing direct context lookup from masquerading as reasoning.

stories.title: BeNice! Closing Looping's Inference-Memory Gap via KV-Sharing
stories.author: Daniel Y. Fu
bullet_points: The paper addresses the memory bottleneck in looped neural network architectures, where repeated inferences cause linear growth in KV-caches.
The proposed solution, 'BeNice!', tackles this by implementing KV-sharing across the depth of recurrent blocks.
The work investigates the property of KV-s, suggesting that the KV-cache from the final recurrence can be shared with earlier ones without sacrificing model quality.

stories.title: Low-Bit N-Gram Embeddings for Language Models
stories.author: Wenyu Du
bullet_points: The paper addresses the high memory cost associated with n-gram embedding tables in modern open-weight language models.
These embedding tables store learned representations of short token sequences (e.g., bigrams/trigrams) to boost model performance.
The research investigates methods to reduce the memory footprint of these n-gram tables without sacrificing performance.

stories.title: Can an Agent Debug a Web Corpus? Agentic Auditing of Slovak FineWeb2
stories.author: Jaroslav Kopčan
bullet_points: Proposes using a Large Language Model (LLM) as a 'corpus debugger' to find failure modes in multilingual NLP datasets like FineWeb2.
The agent interacts with the corpus via a read-only, budgeted API, generating executable tests for human validation.
Demonstrated effectiveness on the Slovak portion of FineWeb2, identifying seven issues across multiple runs.

stories.title: Would an LLM Match into a Residency? Uncertainty, Reasoning and Image Use of Open Language Models on the Spanish MIR Examination
stories.author: Aitor Almeida
bullet_points: The study investigates the reliability of open Large Language Models (LLMs) on the Spanish Medical Residency (MIR) examination.
It moves beyond simple accuracy to assess crucial aspects like uncertainty recognition, clinical reasoning, and image utilization in medical AI.
The research evaluates four open models ranging from 8 to 27 billion parameters to inform safe deployment in healthcare systems.

stories.title: Diffusion Language Models for Perplexity-Aware Black-Box Attacks
stories.author: Suhang Wang
bullet_points: The research introduces diffusion language models for generating perplexity-aware black-box attacks against LLMs.
These attacks operate in a continuous-space latent Gaussian space, mapping back to text via a random mapping and nearest-token lookup.
A key limitation noted is that the resulting prompts are often unnatural and easily detectable by existing input guardrails.

stories.title: An Empirical Study of Recent Large Language Models for Knowledge Graph to Text Generation on Standard Benchmarks
stories.author: Antoine Doucet
bullet_points: The study empirically benchmarks recent Large Language Models (LLMs) against traditional fine-tuned encoder-decoder models for Knowledge Graph-to-Text (KG-to-text) generation.
The research utilizes both reference-based metrics and novel graph-grounded, reference-free LLM-based evaluation validated by human annotations.
Findings indicate that recent LLMs are significantly narrowing the performance gap with established encoder-decoder methods in this task.
